headline: Tigers conquer Australia: Bangladesh win historic Test in Darwin
summary: A dominant nine-wicket victory ends a 23-year wait for a Test win on Australian soil, with Steve Smith admitting the visitors 'outplayed' them.
details: Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, a win that captain Najmul Hossain Shanto described as the biggest victory in the country's cricket history.
The triumph ends a 23-year wait for a Test win in Australia, dating back to their first tour in 2003 where they suffered heavy defeats.
Hasan Mahmud led the attack on the first morning, ripping through the Australian batting line-up with 6-55 to dismiss the hosts for 198.
Tanzid Hasan Tamim made history by scoring the first-ever Test century by a Bangladesh batter in Australia, helping the team pile up 426 runs and create a 228-run lead.
Despite a fighting century from Australia's Cameron Green in the second innings, Mehidy Hasan Miraz took five wickets to ensure the visitors remained in control.
Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque calmly completed the chase, securing a win that Australia captain Pat Cummins and Steve Smith both admitted was deserved.
Unlike previous overseas breakthroughs, this victory was characterized by domination rather than a miracle, with Bangladesh controlling the match across all four days.
caption:
A 23-year wait is over! Bangladesh just dominated Australia on their own soil in a historic Test victory.

Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, a win that captain Najmul Hossain Shanto described as the biggest victory in the country's cricket history.

The triumph ends a 23-year wait for a Test win in Australia, dating back to their first tour in 2003 where they suffered heavy defeats.

Hasan Mahmud led the attack on the first morning, ripping through the Australian batting line-up with 6-55 to dismiss the hosts for 198.

Tanzid Hasan Tamim made history by scoring the first-ever Test century by a Bangladesh batter in Australia, helping the team pile up 426 runs and create a 228-run lead.

Despite a fighting century from Australia's Cameron Green in the second innings, Mehidy Hasan Miraz took five wickets to ensure the visitors remained in control.

Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque calmly completed the chase, securing a win that Australia captain Pat Cummins and Steve Smith both admitted was deserved.

Unlike previous overseas breakthroughs, this victory was characterized by domination rather than a miracle, with Bangladesh controlling the match across all four days.

headline: Govt employees to get new pay scale anytime soon, says PM's principal secy
summary: The structure for the new pay scale is ready and will be implemented within this year, according to PM's Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar.
details: PM's Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar announced that a new pay scale for government employees will be implemented within this year.
Speaking at a press briefing at the Secretariat on Sunday, he confirmed that the entire structure for the new pay scale is ready and the government will make the formal announcement at any time.

Sattar acknowledged that the new pay scale will create economic pressure on the government budget, but stated that the government plans to manage this through the creation of new employment opportunities.
He also noted that the pay scale increase could lead to temporary inflation in the market, a reality that the government will attempt to mitigate through various alternative policies and initiatives.
Additionally, the Principal Secretary addressed the current power and fuel crisis, stating that the current government is not responsible for the situation.
He attributed the crisis to long-term mismanagement and whims of the previous government and assured that sustainable solutions are being implemented to resolve the fuel problem quickly.
caption:
A new pay scale for government employees is coming soon. The structure is ready and will be implemented within this year.

PM's Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar announced that a new pay scale for government employees will be implemented within this year.

Speaking at a press briefing at the Secretariat on Sunday, he confirmed that the entire structure for the new pay scale is ready and the government will make the formal announcement at any time.

Sattar acknowledged that the new pay scale will create economic pressure on the government budget, but stated that the government plans to manage this through the creation of new employment opportunities.

He also noted that the pay scale increase could lead to temporary inflation in the market, a reality that the government will attempt to mitigate through various alternative policies and initiatives.

Additionally, the Principal Secretary addressed the current power and fuel crisis, stating that the current government is not responsible for the situation.

He attributed the crisis to long-term mismanagement and whims of the previous government and assured that sustainable solutions are being implemented to resolve the fuel problem quickly.
